text:
Predicates:
MultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth with siblings.
Siblings(x, y) ::: x has siblings y.
BornTogether(x) ::: x's siblings were born together.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home.
LiveWithStrangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
Premises:
∀x (MultipleBirth(x) → ∀y (Siblings(x, y) → (∃z (Siblings(x, z) ∧ SpendTime(x, z))))) ::: People who are born in a multiple birth with siblings spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (∃y (Siblings(x, y) ∧ BornTogether(y)) → MultipleBirth(x)) ::: If people have siblings who were born together, then they were born in a multiple birth.
∀x (Complain(x) → ∃y (Siblings(x, y) ∧ BornTogether(y))) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who were born together.
∀x (LiveAtHome(x) → ¬LiveWithStrangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (∃y (Siblings(x, y) ∧ SpendTime(x, y))) → LiveAtHome(x) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often live at home.
(MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ LiveWithStrangers(luke)) ⊕ (¬MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬LiveWithStrangers(luke)) ::: Luke either is a baby born in a multiple birth and lives with strangers, or is not a baby born in a multiple birth and does not live with strangers.
Conclusion:
¬MultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬Complain(luke) ::: Luke is neither born in a multiple birth nor complains often about annoying siblings.
